2. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder, the learned Deputy Attorney General, submits that in Arbitration Appeal No. 1 of 1994 the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Narayangonj by Judgment and order dated 18.7.97 affirmed the judgment and order dated 24.11.93 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Narayangonj in Arbitration Suit No. 29 of 1993 and thereafter on 8.8.96 an application for certified copy was tiled an on 14.8.96 the certified copy was made ready for delivery but due to the illness of the tadbirkar-clerk delivery of the same could not be taken before 28.8.96 and then on 5.9.96 the records were sent to the office of the learned Solicitor and since the certified copies of the judgment and order of the trial court were not sent with the records, Deputy Commissioner. Narayangonj was requested on 19.9.96 to sent the same with an opinion of the government pleader. After those were received, the learned ' Solicitor Persed Bhose and on 11.10.96 gave opinion for filing revisional application and then papers were sent to the office of the learned Attorney General and after receiving the same on 21.10.96, it was alloteed to Mr. S.M. Rezaul Karim, the learned assistant Attorney General on 10.11.96 an in the meantime on 31.10.96, the statutory period of limitation already expired. However after allotment the file, the same was misfiled and in spite of best efforts of the office including Mr. Karim, the learned Assistant Attorney General, the file could not be traced out till 15.3.98. Thereafter a draft of the revisional application along with application for condonation of delay was prepared and then affidavit was sworn on 14.5.98 i.e. after delay of 555 days and then the revisional application was sent to the office of the Deputy Attorney General (Civil) on 17.6.98 and on 28.6.98 it was detected that requisite number of needed copies for filing revisional application in a Division Bench was wanting and thereafter the office of the learned Solicitor, after receiving the advices, made required copies and sent back the file to the learned Deputy Attorney General on 19.8.98 who gave file to the learned Assistant Attorney General but again this revisional application was misfiled and instead of best efforts the same could not be traced out and thereafter it is only on 11.7.99 that the same was suddenly found fastened with a bundle of cases pending for hearing and thus another delay of 422 days was caused and in total delay 977 days has been caused in filing this revisional application. The learned Deputy Attorney General next submits that the petitioner, being a Government machinery different agencies are involved in the decision making process and as such the file moves from one of agency to another to get the revisional application ready for filing and there being public interest, the delay, which was caused due to missing of file, may be condoned for ends of justice. 

 3. In his affidavit-in-opposition, the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 denied the material facts and Mr. Md. Helaluddin Mollah, the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 1, submits that in the view of the failure of the petitioner in filing the appeal within the prescribed time, a valuable right has accrued to the plaintiff-opposite party and there is no sufficient cause on the basis of which the application for condonation of delay may be allowed and further no distinction can be made between a private litigation and the government and negligence of the servant of the government is not a sufficient cause within the meaning of section 5 of the Limitation Act.
